cases.name: Connie Lynette Crow Simmons
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Connie loved any chance to get together with family and friends to laugh and share a meal. Some of her most favorite things to do were road trips on the fly and her love for being outdoors during all of the changing seasons.

Connie was a child of God and had deep faith in her Lord. She had an innate compassion and empathy for others. Connie had the most generous loving heart, befriended everyone and always put others before herself without a moment’s hesitation. She was a beautiful soul with a bright smile and amazing strength. Anyone that knew Connie will remember her always telling you that she loved you! She will be remembered and live on through the hearts and lives that she has touched in her lifetime."

https://www.hamiltonsfuneralhome.com/services/services_detail.aspx?rid=53077

"Asked what she'll remember most about her sister Connie Simmons, Katosha Crow said it's impossible to narrow down. "Me and my sister had never been apart from each other longer than when she spent three years in another state when we were kids, and since then we’ve been in each other’s lives every day," Crow said. "I’m going to miss everything." "Even if she saw you yesterday, she’d just grab you and hug you," she said, wiping her eyes. "Or maybe she just knew I needed a hug." Connie Simmons' daughter, Jordin Young, said her mother had been a "wonderful" person for her family and everyone else she knew. "She loved everybody and everybody loved her," she said. "I miss my mom dearly."

https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/crime-and-courts/2021/07/23/iowa-murder-connie-simmons-des-moines-man-datron-simmons-sentenced-50-years/8064325002/

cases.name: Nohema Marie Castillo y Castillo Graber
cases.about:
She taught Spanish at Fairfield High School. After graduating from school, Graber became a flight attendant with now-defunct Mexicana de Aviación, then her home country's oldest airline. But she wasn't satisfied so she did something wholly unexpected, according to Paul Graber.  She began to studying to be a commercial airline pilot. She paid her way through flight school and became one of the first women in Mexico licensed to fly passenger jets. As their children grew older, Nohema Graber decided, in her fifties, to get a degree in English and a teaching certificate from Iowa Wesleyan University in nearby Mt. Pleasant. Nohema Graber had expected her English degree would turn into a job as an English teacher. But when she graduated from Iowa Wesleyan in 2006, Spanish teachers were in demand. And she was a native speaker. Her first job as a teacher was at Ottumwa High School where she taught until 2012. When a part-time job opened for a teacher at Fairfield High School, she took it in hopes it could become full-time, Paul Graber said. It did. She had become a fixture at Fairfield High School, loved by many students. She often received cards and letters from former students, Paul Graber said. 

https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2021/11/05/iowa-spanish-teacher-nohema-graber-mourned-murder-charges-for-teens/6302069001/
cases.narrative:
On 11/3/2021, police found her body in Chautauqua City Park under a tarp, wheelbarrow and railroad ties. She had been beaten to death with a baseball bat. 

Ms. Graber drove after school to the park – where she would always go on her daily walk. She left her vehicle at around 4pm in the parking lot.

At some point during her walk, the pair of teens allegedly ambushed her with a baseball bat and dealt the fatal blows.
